justification: PDDL problem instances, correct plans, and validators are all openly released and machine-checkable, but classical Blocksworld/Logistics planning is a decades-old, extensively documented AI subfield with heavy pretraining-corpus presence.

All 2,860 questions and gold labels across 8 ToM task types are released openly on GitHub as a fixed static set; social-cognition/false-belief scenarios are less common in typical web/pretraining text than generic QA, giving moderate novelty.

Instances and answers are fully released, but they are algorithmically generated narratives (murder mysteries, team allocations) unlikely to appear verbatim anywhere in pretraining corpora, and the free-text-reasoning-over-narrative format is atypical for standard benchmarks.

Train/dev questions and answers are public, but the original official leaderboard held out hidden test-set answers; implicit multi-hop commonsense trivia has been extensively replicated and discussed since 2021, giving it low remaining novelty.

The dataset, generator code, and gold kinship-relation labels are fully public and static, but synthetic templated family-relation stories are an unusual, low-natural-frequency text domain relative to typical corpora.

Dev-set questions/answers are public but the official CodaLab leaderboard's test-set gold answers are held out; multi-hop Wikipedia QA is one of the most heavily used and cited QA formats since 2018, so contamination risk from dev-set exposure is high.

Dev-set answers are public but AI2's official leaderboard withholds test-set gold answers; Wikipedia-paragraph numerical reasoning QA has been a standard eval since 2019 with very high cumulative web/paper exposure.

All question-answer pairs across train/valid/test are released openly with no hidden leaderboard; grounding in full books/movie scripts is a less common QA format than generic passage QA, though the source narratives themselves (public-domain and popular books) may be individually memorized to varying degrees.

Code, environments, and evaluation harness (MARBLE) are fully open source with no hidden answer key; because scores emerge from live multi-agent interaction (negotiation, Werewolf, cooperative building) rather than static lookup of a fixed answer, outcomes vary run-to-run and cannot be memorized the way a fixed Q&A pair can, despite the scenario set itself not rotating.
